paragraphs: Children in Leicestershire County Council's care live with carers approved by the council's own fostering service or by independent agencies such as those listed on this page. The council says it has more than 700 children in its care, with a wide range of needs, talents and backgrounds, and its children and family services were rated outstanding by Ofsted in 2024.

To foster with the county you need to be 21 or over, and there is no upper age limit. You can be single, married or in a relationship (couples need to have lived together for at least a year), working or not, and you can rent rather than own your home. A child needs a spare bedroom of their own, although babies can sleep in your room and brothers and sisters can share. You will also need some childcare experience and a good support network.

The council sets out the route in stages: an initial visit at home, then around two months of checks, references and its Skills to Foster course, followed by about four months with your own assessing social worker before your application goes to panel. Approved carers receive an allowance for each child, ongoing training and support from the fostering team around the clock.

If you live in or around towns such as Loughborough, Hinckley, Coalville or Market Harborough, speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies below, and compare the allowances, training and local support each one offers before you apply.

sources.title: How to become a foster carer with us (Leicestershire County Council)
